problem: Embodied AI benchmarks are polarized between isolated-skill tests (navigation, manipulation) and heavy full-household simulations. None evaluates mobile cleaning robots that combine sweeping and grasping (dual-mode) on structured multi-target cleaning tasks.
motivation: Dual-mode mobile cleaning robots are becoming commercially realistic, but there is no reproducible, lightweight, task-centric benchmark with metrics for coverage, task success, motion quality and computation. A middle-ground testbed is needed to compare heuristic, planning and learning agents.
key_idea: CleanUpBench is an Isaac Sim benchmark for a mobile robot with a sweeping module and a 6-DOF arm. It offers 20 hand-designed scenes across 5 categories plus procedural generation, single- and multi-robot settings, and a multi-level metric suite (TCR, CR, SR, ME, collisions, CT, FT, kinematics).
insight: The decomposed TCR (sweep vs grasp) lets single-mode and dual-mode agents be compared fairly, and it shows sweep-only methods get 0 grasp success while grasp-only methods get 0 sweep success. Only PRIMAL2, a multi-agent path-finding RL method, reaches balanced dual-mode performance (TCR 0.60), while CA-DRL fails completely with 81 collisions. No method is strong across all metrics, and the appendix reports CR and TCR correlated at r=0.81. Caveat: the baselines are adapted from unrelated tasks, and the tables contain internal inconsistencies (e.g. 5 vs 20 runs, 250 vs 300 s, and a 'ten' vs 'eight' method count).
method: Robot platform: wheeled base with a front sweeping brush and a 6-DOF arm with a parallel gripper. Sensors are RGB-D, LiDAR and segmentation; the hybrid action space is mode {sweep, grasp, navigate} × velocity × arm joint velocities.

Scenes: 20 hand-designed scenes in 5 categories (sparse, dense sweeping, narrow corridor, dynamic obstacles, multi-zone), 4 each. Sweepable objects (0.01-0.05 kg) and graspable objects (0.1-0.8 kg) have physical properties set in Isaac Sim 4.5 / PhysX.

Procedural generation: Voronoi/room layout, Poisson-disk obstacle sampling, A* connectivity check, and pattern-based target placement (random, clustered, linear). Yields an unseen scene for generalization.

Metric suite: Coverage Ratio, Sweep Redundancy, Task Completion Ratio = α·TCR_sweep + β·TCR_grasp (0.5/0.5), Motion Efficiency (path length per completed target), collision count, computation time, finish time, and velocity/acceleration/jerk.

Protocol: random spawn, randomized object placement, fixed time budget (300 s), single-robot or up to 3-robot settings, and a standard interface for planners, heuristic/FSM controllers and RL policies.
Baselines: Manhattan/Chebyshev/Vertical/Horizontal coverage, m-explore, CA-DRL, IR2, BHyRL, REMANI, PRIMAL2, adapted to sweep-only, grasp-only or dual-mode.

setting.backbone: Benchmark paper; baselines are heuristic planners (Manhattan, Chebyshev, Vertical, Horizontal, m-explore), RL policies (CA-DRL, IR2, BHyRL, PRIMAL2) and the REMANI planner
setting.training_data: Benchmark paper; RL baselines' training data is not described
setting.observation: RGB-D 640×480, semantic segmentation, 360° LiDAR (1440 points), 12-D proprioception, target locations and completion status
setting.action_space: hybrid: discrete mode {sweep, grasp, navigate} + continuous linear/angular velocity [-1,1]^2 + 6-DOF arm joint velocities
setting.privileged: Task information (target locations and completion status) is exposed in the observation space; high-level perception (segmentation, affordance maps) is optional

numbers_note: CleanUpBench is a new benchmark not in the canonical list and its metrics (TCR, CR, SR, ME) are not standard navigation metrics, so the baseline results are not recorded as the paper's own method numbers (all methods are baselines). The main results are in Table 'Baseline method performance on CleanUpBench' (e.g. PRIMAL2 TCR 0.60, CR 0.69).
results: Among ten baselines, PRIMAL2 is best overall (TCR 0.60, TCR_S 0.50, TCR_G 0.70, CR 0.69, 0.04 collisions), ahead of REMANI (TCR 0.30) and Chebyshev/Horizontal (TCR 0.15). Sweep-only methods have low redundancy (SR 0.01) but zero grasping. CA-DRL fails (TCR 0.00, 81 collisions) despite the highest velocity of 1.12 m/s.
limitations: Scenes are idealized (limited textures, lighting and dynamics), sensing has no noise, and interaction outcomes are binary/deterministic

Baselines are adapted from other tasks and there is no learned dual-mode agent trained on the benchmark; the generalization (procedural) results are only described qualitatively, and numbers are inconsistent across sections (5 vs 20 runs, 250 vs 300 s, scene counts)
Not yet released (code promised on acceptance); no language/foundation-model tasks or real-robot validation
